project.title: DP-PFN: Differentially Private Prior-Data Fitted Networks
project.domain: differential privacy / prior-data fitted networks / machine learning

question.text: How can prior-data fitted networks (TabPFN, NodePFN) be used for differentially private tabular and graph prediction so that weights cost no privacy budget, while certificates come from black-box wrappers or noise-aware post-processing rather than from training loss?

hypotheses.text: If PFN weights are trained only on synthetic prior data and preprocessing is shard-local or public, privacy accounting reduces to the context release. A black-box Vote/LogPool/Student wrapper, or a noise-aware reader of an already-private summary S=M(D), is (ε,δ)-DP regardless of approximation error (Prop. 0, Cor. B4, Thm. D1).
hypotheses.evidence: Prop. 0 and the wrapper/post-processing guarantees are correct (X0). Must add a third route: certified-by-architecture PFNs (PrivTab, arXiv 2610.10068). TREDBench caveat: synthetic-task selection uses real data.

hypotheses.text: No bound on PFN training loss certifies worst-case DP (Prop. B2). On closed-form floored priors, the log-gap Λ(D) and row-sensitivity s(θ,n) stay small on prior-typical datasets but can be driven large on adversarial neighbouring pairs; a more accurate PFN leaks more unless the training target itself is private (Obs. B5).
hypotheses.evidence: E1-lite: Lambda small on typical data and larger adversarially (supported); network leakage exceeds the exact mechanism's worst case by up to ~2.5x in support (supported: exact-PPD privacy is not inherited); but leakage stayed below 2B_y everywhere searched (the 'driven large' part not observed for a small LayerNorm network); better-trained PFNs leak more (Obs. B5 supported).

hypotheses.text: At fixed ε, DP-PFN-Vote sample size n* is set by teacher error e(m) at small shard size m (Thm. C2). A PFN teacher therefore attains a smaller n* than per-shard trained PATE teachers, and the minimizing m matches the C2 prediction.
hypotheses.source: proposal Section 4; tested by E2, E3
hypotheses.evidence: E3-lite (idealised Gaussian prior, exact-Bayes teacher): PFN-like teachers lower DP-Vote error at small n*eps, and C2 picks m within 2x. But C2 must be pointwise (bias floor 13-16% at m=2) and its n* is conservative by ~2-10x. Real PFN teachers and tuned/charged trained teachers still to test (E2/E3).

hypotheses.text: A PFN trained with the release mechanism inside the prior matches the private-data posterior predictive. Versus naive TabPFN on the same release, it reduces under-confidence on label randomized response and over-confidence on bulk DP synthetic rows, lowering NLL and ECE at the same ε (Thm. D1, Prop. D2).
hypotheses.source: proposal Section 5; tested by E4, Gate 2
hypotheses.evidence: Label RR: a trained noise-aware PFN recovers 71-86% of the exact NLL gain over naive plug-in (E4-lite). Synthetic data: the sign of naive mis-calibration depends on the generator. It is under-confident for a noisy full histogram (D2-sparse, exact targets) and over-confident in 12/12 cells for a marginal-based, naive-Bayes-structured synthesizer (E4b-lite, trained networks: +0.081 to +0.186), where non-private naive Bayes is already over-confident (+0.098 to +0.165) and extra synthetic rows add little (+0.003 to +0.040). In E4b-lite the trained noise-aware PFN is calibrated (|over-confidence| <= 0.014) and lowers NLL in 12/12 cells. E4c-lite spends half the budget on 15 feature-pair tables chosen by label informativeness (a star, not a dependence-selected MST tree): naive over-confidence rises in 8/12 cells (by up to +0.061) because the split budget adds noise and the star recovers little correlation; the noise-aware PFN stays in -0.008..+0.025 and lowers NLL in 12/12 cells. E4c-prime selects a per-dataset tree privately, as MST does: at n<=128, eps<=16 the selection is close to random, and even a non-private oracle tree lowers naive over-confidence only at n=128 with eps=4-16 (3/12 cells), because splitting the budget adds more noise than the tree removes. The noise-aware PFN stays calibrated on the DP-MST release and beats naive in NLL in 12/12 cells, though that release is less informative than E4b's. An n*eps sweep (n 32-8192, eps 1-64) puts the crossover at n*eps ~ 8,000: below ~2,000 plain feature-label margins beat every tree release; from 32,768 the private tree wins every cell by ~0.1 nats and removes the +0.08 structural over-confidence that plain margins keep. Bulk synthetic rows matter in the k -> inf limit (+0.32 to +0.41 over-confidence at n*eps <= 128 vs +0.11 to +0.18 for k=1). E4d-lite: a noise-aware PFN reading the noisy tables is calibrated from n=32 to 8192 (-0.010 to +0.019), beats the plain release's own classifier in 20/20 cells and the tree release's in 14/20, removes plain margins' structural over-confidence, and prefers the tree release from n*eps = 8192. Trained 3x longer (18k steps) it beats the tree release's own classifier in 18/20 cells and is within -0.011..+0.003 nats of it at n*eps >= 32,768. Open: real data, TabPFN scale.

history.text: Proposal read end-to-end (25 pages). Hypotheses H1–H4 registered from Sections 1–5. No experiment has been run; E1–E8 remain planned. Background citations in the PDF were not re-checked by the authors.

Plan reviewed: theory audit (X0), citation audit + related work (PrivTab, Private PoEtry, TabPATE overlap), and four CPU pilots (E1-lite, E3-lite, D2-check, G3-check). See reviews/2026-11-05-plan-review.md.
Independent rerun on a second machine (gpu-gfkd; commit 8f95ca4 logs) reproduced E1 training exactly and E1/E3/D2/G3 numbers within sampling noise.

E4-lite: A trained noise-aware PFN on label-RR releases recovers 71-86% of the exact noise-aware NLL gain over naive plug-in at n=128 (NLL 0.623/0.575/0.554 vs naive 0.644/0.604/0.565), with unchanged accuracy and no cost on clean data (max NLL difference 0.0002). The naive PFN matches the exact naive target (KL <= 0.0013), i.e. it is under-confident as Prop. D2 predicts. Gate 2: pass (pilot, label RR only).
D2-sparse (project author, gpu-gfkd): with a sparse full-histogram release, naive synthetic-data use is under-confident, not over-confident; the noise-aware target still lowers NLL in every cell.

E4b-lite: Marginal-based DP synthesizer (d=16, 12 cells): naive PFN on synthetic rows is over-confident in 12, under-confident in 0 and calibrated in 0 cells (largest +0.186 at n=32, eps=1, k=4); quadrupling the synthetic rows changes its over-confidence by +0.003 to +0.040. The noise-aware PFN lowers NLL in 12/12 cells (gain +0.031 to +0.145 nats), with |over-confidence| <= 0.014 and accuracy within 0.016 of naive.

E4c-lite: Same budget as E4b, half spent on 15 (x_u, x_v, y) pair tables along a star chosen by label informativeness (not MST's dependence selection; the star's edges are no more correlated than random pairs). Naive over-confidence rises in 8/12 cells (+0.008 to +0.061) and is flat or lower in the rest (-0.012 to +0.001). The noise-aware PFN stays in -0.008..+0.025 and lowers NLL in 12/12 cells (0.026 to 0.205). Run on gpu-gfkd by the project author.

E4c-prime: Per-dataset DP MST selection (eps/3 each for label tables, selection and pair tables; 12 cells paired with E4b, 12/12 verified): private selection picks edges barely more correlated than random pairs (-0.001 to +0.051 |corr|; 0.21 vs oracle 0.29 at n=128, eps=16). Relative to E4b's release, naive over-confidence is lower in only 2/12 cells for the DP tree, 3/12 for the star and 3/12 even for a non-private oracle tree; at n=128, eps=16 the oracle tree lowers it by 0.017-0.019. The DP tree costs naive use 0.004-0.086 accuracy. The noise-aware PFN on the DP-MST release stays calibrated (-0.016 to +0.015) and beats naive in NLL in 12/12 cells, but is worse than E4b's noise-aware PFN on the simpler release in 12/12 cells (by 0.002-0.069 nats).

E4c-prime sweep: n*eps sweep (n 32-8192, eps 1-64, 20 cells): the release's own classifier (k -> inf limit of naive use) gains from a tree once n*eps >= 8192 for the non-private oracle tree and >= 32768 for the private per-dataset MST tree (all cells at and above, NLL); below ~2,000 every tree release is worse than plain feature-label margins. Private selection becomes informative near n*eps 2,000 and near-oracle by 8,000-33,000. Plain marginals keep a structural over-confidence of +0.075 to +0.087 at n*eps >= 32,768 that only the tree removes (noise-free TAN beats noise-free NB by 0.055-0.122 nats for n >= 128). At n*eps <= 128 the plug-in is far more over-confident than the PFN on k=1 rows (+0.321 to +0.412 vs +0.111 to +0.181), so bulk synthetic rows matter when k is large.

E4d-lite: Noise-aware PFN reading the noisy tables (n 32-8192, 20 cells): calibrated everywhere (over-confidence -0.010 to +0.019) and better in NLL than the release's own classifier in 20/20 cells (plain release) and 14/20 (tree release). At n*eps >= 32,768 it removes plain margins' structural over-confidence (-0.008..+0.005 vs +0.076..+0.087 for the naive-Bayes plug-in). The noise-aware analyst prefers the tree release in every cell from n*eps = 8192.0; at n <= 128 the table reader is within -0.036..-0.001 (plain) and -0.053..-0.000 (tree) nats of the row-reading noise-aware PFNs.

E4d-lite longer training: Training the table-reading noise-aware PFN 3x longer (6k -> 18k steps, warm start): at n*eps >= 32,768 its gap to the tree release's own classifier goes from +0.007..+0.025 (6k) to +0.003..+0.027 (12k) to -0.011..+0.003 (18k) nats; closed in 4/6 cells. Over all 20 cells at 18k: beats the plain release's classifier in 20/20 and the tree release's in 18/20; over-confidence -0.008..+0.022; NLL change vs 6k -0.023..+0.002 (tree) and -0.003..+0.000 (plain).

experiments.title: Numerical audit of all proposal constants; exact one-draw privacy loss
experiments.summary: All constants reproduce. Thm A2 tight for the posterior draw (2.193 vs 2B_y=2.197 at n=1000); the clean-target release (A5) costs ~B_y, half the bound; a noisy-PPD label costs 0.0034 at n=1000. Prop. G3 threshold for the worked example is 290 (dense SNR), not 311.

experiments.title: Exact vs amortized privacy loss of a small PFN on a floored logistic prior
experiments.summary: Trained PFN (excess NLL 0.0006 over exact Bayes): on prior-typical data its label-DP leakage tracks the exact PPD's (median ratio 0.84-1.42; gap Lambda median <= 0.21). Gradient search finds in-support neighbours where it leaks 1.2-2.5x the exact mechanism's worst case, and the gap grows out of support (Lambda up to 2.24). Largest leakage found 1.79, below 2B_y in every setting. An under-trained checkpoint leaks 0.10-1.40x the exact level (Obs. B5).

experiments.title: Theorem C2 vs simulation; Bayes vs trained teachers; Vote vs LogPool
experiments.summary: Exact-Bayes (PFN-like) teachers beat trained logistic-regression teachers under DP-Vote by +4.1/+3.7/+2.3 points at eps=0.1 (n=250/500/1000); the gap vanishes at large n*eps. Even Bayes teachers leave a 13-16% infinite-T error floor at m=2, so C2 must be pointwise. C2 argmax m is within 2x of the observed best in 42/45 configs, but its n* (1,176-5,077) is very conservative. LogPool loses to Vote by up to 7.5 points with calibrated teachers.

experiments.title: Naive vs noise-aware use of label-RR and DP synthetic data (exact Bayes)
experiments.summary: Label RR: naive is under-confident, growing with n (n=1000, eps=0.5: ECE 0.165 vs 0.068, over-confidence -0.159 vs -0.001); noise-aware fixes it at equal accuracy. DP synthetic data: naive over-confident only at n=50 (+0.032) in a 2-parameter model.

experiments.title: Trained noise-aware PFN vs naive PFN on label-RR releases
experiments.summary: A trained noise-aware PFN on label-RR releases recovers 71-86% of the exact noise-aware NLL gain over naive plug-in at n=128 (NLL 0.623/0.575/0.554 vs naive 0.644/0.604/0.565), with unchanged accuracy and no cost on clean data (max NLL difference 0.0002). The naive PFN matches the exact naive target (KL <= 0.0013), i.e. it is under-confident as Prop. D2 predicts.

experiments.title: Naive vs noise-aware use of a sparse 512-cell DP histogram (exact Bayes)
experiments.summary: Full-histogram release (Laplace(2/eps), 512 cells, 5n rows): naive use is under-confident in 8 of 9 cells (down to -0.188 at n=200, eps=1), over-confident only at n=50, eps=0.5. The noise-aware target lowers NLL in every cell (by up to 0.098). Run on gpu-gfkd by the project author.

experiments.title: Trained noise-aware PFN vs naive PFN on high-dimensional, marginal-based DP synthetic data
experiments.summary: Marginal-based DP synthesizer (d=16, 12 cells): naive PFN on synthetic rows is over-confident in 12, under-confident in 0 and calibrated in 0 cells (largest +0.186 at n=32, eps=1, k=4); quadrupling the synthetic rows changes its over-confidence by +0.003 to +0.040. The noise-aware PFN lowers NLL in 12/12 cells (gain +0.031 to +0.145 nats), with |over-confidence| <= 0.014 and accuracy within 0.016 of naive.

experiments.title: Spectral recovery on edge-RR SBMs vs threshold formulas
experiments.summary: Simulation follows the dense spiked-matrix SNR (variance p'(1-p')); thresholds 59/290/2739 at eps=1/2/4. At N=1024, eps=2 structural signal is gone (overlap 0.04).
